sources.citation: Chacko, Sajayan, Juliana Kelsall & Liahey Ngwazah. 2012. Sociolinguistic survey of selected Rajasthani speech varieties of Rajasthan, India, Volume 6: Marwari, Merwari, and Godwari. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-034. 58 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: SILENT. Sociolinguistic survey with 210-item wordlists (Godwari sites Kherwa and Falna in Pali, Bagra in Jalore; RTT story from Bagseen, Sirohi); no phonology chapter and no stress marks. Sec. 1.2: Godwari circuit = Jalore, Pali, Sirohi; 'four main varieties called Balvi, Khuni, Sirohi and Madahaddi'. Sec. 1.4 names Gusain 2004 (Marwari) as the only grammatical description.

sources.note: Nothing; a footnote only: 'In Godwari, Bhitrauti and other languages of south-east Rajasthan, an adverb agreeing in gender and number with the direct object.. is used to express perfective aspect. See Hook 1982 and Hook and Chauhan 1986.'

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1908. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Part II: Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group: Specimens of the Rajasthani and Gujarati. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. pp. 87-89 'Godwari', pp. 90-91 'Sirohi'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: SILENT. Godwari section gives only segmental pronunciation notes (e fully pronounced; ch > s; s > h), Gujarati/Malvi borrowings and a Prodigal Son specimen; Sirohi section likewise (aspiration neglected, cerebral as dental, neuter gender). The volume's only accent remark is the general transliteration note (p. 3) that an acute marks an accented syllable when necessary; none is used in the Godwari/Sirohi specimens.
